## From Passive "Restoration" to Intentional Ecosystem Design

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-warning icon=false}
### The Passive "Restoration" Pitfall

- **The Myth of Self-Assembly:** Traditional stream restoration assumes dropping in structural channel tweaks (BDAs, boulder clusters, Stage 0) will magically cause the river to "restore itself."
- **Flawed Metrics:** Success is measured by *inputs* ("dollars spent") and *outputs* ("feet of bank shaped on Day 1") rather than functional performance.
- **Unmonitored Greenwashing:** In a heavily managed snowmelt river, unmonitored structural fixes fail to deliver downstream thermal or water quality gains.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}
### The Designer Ecosystem Approach

- **Acknowledge Human Control:** "We must embrace *Designer Ecosystems*—admitting that humans control these systems and explicitly designing them for specific ecological goals, rather than hoping passive restoration fixes itself" (*Ross et al. 2015, Ann. Rev. Environ. Resour.*).
- **Target Real Levers:** Direct investment toward explicit functional outcomes: flow preservation, riparian shading, and diversion connectivity.
- **Continuous Sensor Arrays:** Real-time sensor monitoring ($\text{Temp, DO, Turbidity, NO}_3^-$) provides unassailable design feedback.
:::

:::
:::

## What Works vs. What Doesn't: Evidence Matrix

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(dplyr)

matrix_data <- data.frame(
  Technique = c(
    "Dam / Diversion Removal & Retrofits",
    "Active Riparian Canopy (Willow/Cottonwood)",
    "Floodplain & Side-Channel Reconnection",
    "In-Stream Reconfiguration (ELJs, Boulders)",
    "Beaver Dam Analogues (BDAs)",
    "Stage 0 / Process-Based Restoration"
  ),
  `Physical Mechanism` = c(
    "Restores longitudinal connectivity, natural sediment transport, & thermal regime.",
    "Solar radiation shading, bank root cohesion, hyporheic nutrient uptake.",
    "Attenuates peak flood energy, drops TSS, expands hyporheic residence.",
    "Creates localized velocity refuge, scour pools, & physical trout habitat.",
    "Aggrades channel, forces overbank flooding, elevates alluvial water table.",
    "Spreads flow into unconfined multi-thread wetland complexes."
  ),
  `Downstream WQ Evidence` = c(
    "<span class='badge badge-high'>HIGH EVIDENCE</span><br/>Eliminates local temp spikes, re-oxygenates, clears fine sediment.",
    "<span class='badge badge-high'>HIGH (THERMAL)</span><br/>Consistent 1–3°C drop in max summer water temps. Moderate NO3- interception.",
    "<span class='badge badge-mod'>MODERATE</span><br/>High TSS & NO3- settling during flood peaks; negligible during baseflows.",
    "<span class='badge badge-low'>LOW / NEGLIGIBLE</span><br/>High local physical habitat score; zero downstream nutrient/thermal impact.",
    "<span class='badge badge-mixed'>MIXED / CONDITIONAL</span><br/>Local TSS drop, but frequently spikes summer max temps (solar ponding) & releases Ortho-P.",
    "<span class='badge badge-low'>UNPROVEN WQ</span><br/>High local habitat value in low-energy valley bottoms; unproven for downstream export."
  ),
  `Long-Term Viability` = c(
    "Permanent solution. Highest ROI per linear km.",
    "High durability once established; self-sustaining.",
    "High viability if high-flow flood hydrograph remains intact.",
    "Vulnerable to destruction during 10-year snowmelt runoff events.",
    "High failure rate in high-energy gravel rivers without real beavers.",
    "Requires huge land footprint; high evaporative loss."
  ),
  `Primary Citations` = c(
    "Bednarek (2001)<br/>Doyle et al. (2005)<br/>Bernhardt & Palmer (2011)",
    "Poole & Berman (2001)<br/>Caissie (2006)<br/>Kalny et al. (2017)",
    "Opperman et al. (2010)<br/>Noe et al. (2013)<br/>Kaushal et al. (2008)",
    "Palmer et al. (2005, 2010)<br/>Bernhardt et al. (2005)<br/>Filoso & Palmer (2011)",
    "Weber et al. (2017)<br/>Lautz et al. (2013)<br/>Majerova et al. (2015)",
    "Cluer & Thorne (2014)<br/>Powers et al. (2019)<br/>Kondolf et al. (2006)"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

matrix_data %>%
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l")) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = TRUE,
    position = "center",
    font_size = 13
  ) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#0f766e", color = "white", bold = TRUE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "410px", width = "100%")
```

::: {.callout-note icon=false style="margin-top: 10px;"}
**Ecosystem Design Principle:** Rather than assuming passive channel form will fix itself, intentional ecosystem design targets direct physical levers (flow preservation, thermal shading, barrier retrofits) with continuous monitoring feedback (*Ross et al. 2015, Ann. Rev. Environ. Resour.*).
:::

## Mindful Stewardship & Risk Mitigation ($100M Settlement)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.ross-card}
### The "3% Sentinel Rule"

Institute a mandatory policy requiring every funded capital project to dedicate **3% to 5% of its total budget** to automated continuous sensor monitoring.

- **Design Feedback Loop:** Operationalizes the *Designer Ecosystems* framework (*Ross et al. 2015*) by measuring explicit performance goals.
- **Pre- & Post-Implementation:** 12-month pre-project baseline and 3-year post-project continuous tracking.
- **Continuous Telemetry:** Automated stations deployed upstream & downstream of project reaches.
- **Beyond Grab Samples:** Replaces monthly manual grab samples that miss 90%+ of runoff and thermal events.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.ross-card}
### Fiduciary Protection for Committee

1. **Unassailable Accountability:** Empirical proof of performance demonstrating ROI to stakeholders and regulators.
2. **Early Risk Mitigation:** Identifies underperforming or failing interventions early so management can adapt.
3. **Shield Against Greenwashing:** Defends committee funding choices with open, real-time science-backed data.
:::

:::
:::

Focus on **Water Flows & Aquatic Habitat via Diversion Retrofits**. Engineered fish passage & bypass flow structures between Munroe Canal & South Platte solve passage, thermal & habitat constraints together.

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
4. Best Projects for Flow Regime?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
**Active Hydrograph Management**: Diversion consolidation, seasonal water-sharing leases, and automated bypass gates. Channel tweaks cannot replace missing summer water.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
5. Committee's Biggest Bang for Buck?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
**Riparian Canopy Re-establishment & Diversion Bypass Retrofits**. Native willow/cottonwood shading yields guaranteed thermal drops (1–3°C) at a fraction of heavy equipment cost.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-title}
6. Key Stakeholders to Engage?
